Title: Photosynthesis in Green Plants

## Learning Objectives
- Students will be able to define photosynthesis.
- Students will be able to explain the role of chlorophyll.
- Students will be able to write the overall equation of photosynthesis.

## What is Photosynthesis
Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water using light energy. It takes place mainly in the leaves.

For example, a sunflower growing in a garden uses sunlight to make the sugar it needs to grow.

## The Role of Chlorophyll
Chlorophyll is a green pigment that absorbs red and blue light. It is found in chloroplasts, the small structures inside leaf cells.

Remember that without chlorophyll a plant cannot capture light energy.

## The Overall Equation
Carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O) react to form glucose (C6H12O6) and oxygen (O2).

6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2

For example, a leaf in bright light releases oxygen bubbles when placed under water.

## Summary
Photosynthesis turns light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. Chlorophyll captures the light, and oxygen is released as a by-product.

## Review Questions
- What is photosynthesis?
- Where in the leaf cell is chlorophyll found?
- What are the products of photosynthesis?
